stem:
The brightness of some stars varies regularly. These stars are called variable stars.

Fig. 2.1 shows the variation of luminosity with time for a variable star.

[[fig:f1]]

A student determines the period *T* and mean luminosity *L* of the star.

The student repeats the process for different variable stars.

It is suggested that *L* and *T* are related by the equation

*L* = *S K T*ᵃ

where *S* is the luminosity of the Sun, and *a* and *K* are constants.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A graph is plotted as lg *L* on the y-axis against lg *T* on the x-axis.

Determine expressions for the gradient and y-intercept.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Values of *T* and *L* are given in Table 2.1.

[[fig:f2]]

Calculate and record values of lg (*T* / days) and lg (*L* / 10³⁰ W) in Table 2.1. Include the absolute uncertainties in lg (*L* / 10³⁰ W).

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Plot a graph of lg (*L* / 10³⁰ W) against lg (*T* / days).

Include error bars for lg (*L* / 10³⁰ W).

[[fig:f3]]

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the straight line of best fit and a worst acceptable straight line on your graph. Label both lines.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the gradient of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Determine the y-intercept of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Using your answers to (a), (c)(iii) and (c)(iv), determine the values of *a* and *K*. Include the absolute uncertainties in your values. You need not be concerned with units.

Data: *S* = 3.85 × 10²⁶ W

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
A variable star has a period of 5.0 days.

Determine the luminosity *L* of this star.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1
figures.alt: A variable star's luminosity varies with time, with two successive peaks marked to show the period.

figures.caption: Table 2.1
figures.alt: A table of values of T in days and L in 10³⁰ W, with empty columns for lg (T / days) and lg (L / 10³⁰ W).
A blank graph grid with lg (T / days) on the horizontal axis and lg (L / 10³⁰ W) on the vertical axis.
